description: This line plot illustrates the relationship between three distinct accuracy metrics—Final Accuracy, Δ Accuracy, and Initial Accuracy—and varying levels of initial confidence. The x-axis is labeled 'Initial Confidence' and employs a linear scale ranging from approximately 0.81 to 0.99, with tick marks appearing at intervals of 0.01, except for the omission of the 0.83 mark. The y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy' and also uses a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 1.0, with major gridlines and tick labels marked at intervals of 0.2. The plot features three distinct lines: the 'Final Accuracy' is represented by a blue solid line with square markers, starting near 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.81, remaining consistently above 0.85 across the range, and ending slightly above 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.99. The 'Δ Accuracy' is shown as an orange dashed line with diamond markers, beginning at approximately 0.45 at an initial confidence of 0.81, exhibiting a generally decreasing trend with some fluctuations, and concluding near 0.05 at an initial confidence of 0.99. The 'Initial Accuracy' is depicted by a green dashed line with circular markers, initiating at approximately 0.55 at an initial confidence of 0.81, showing fluctuations before gradually rising to stabilize near 0.95 at an initial confidence of 0.99. All three lines are accompanied by error bars indicating variability at each data point, with the blue line demonstrating the smallest error bars for most of the data range. A legend at the top of the plot clearly associates each line style and color with its respective metric.
caption_used: This line plot illustrates the relationship between different accuracies and initial confidence. The x-axis is labeled 'Initial Confidence,' with a linear scale ranging from approximately 0.81 to 0.99, with tick intervals at every 0.01 except 0.83. The y-axis is labeled 'Accuracy,' also on a linear scale, with a range from 0.0 to 1.0, marked at intervals of 0.2. There are three lines: a blue solid line with square markers representing 'Final Accuracy,' which starts near 1.0 at an initial confidence of 0.81, maintains a relatively high level throughout, and ends slightly above 1.0 at 0.99. An orange dashed line with diamond markers represents 'Δ Accuracy,' starting around 0.45, showing consistent growth throughout, and finally rising to approximately 0.3. Lastly, a green dashed line with circular markers represents 'Initial Accuracy,' beginning approximately 0.55 at an initial confidence of 0.81, fluctuating in value, and finally stabilizing near 0.95. Each line visually presents changes in accuracy corresponding to initial confidence values. All three lines include error bars, indicating variability at each data point, with the blue line having the least variability for most of the data points. There are legends provided on top of the plot to match different line styles to their labels.
